a: A value that can change while the program is running
A value that is fixed and can never change
The name of the program
A single line of code
tasks.fb: The name stays the same, but the value inside it can be replaced.

a: Adds 5 to the value already in total, then stores the new value back in total
Checks whether total is equal to total plus 5
Creates a second variable also called total
Always sets total to 5
tasks.fb: A single equals sign assigns a value; it never compares.

a: A named value that is fixed when the program is written and cannot change as it runs
A variable with a very short name
A value stored on the hard disk
A value that changes every time the program runs
tasks.fb: Constants are set once; variables can be reassigned.

tasks.q: Which of these is best stored as a constant in a game?
a: The number of lives the player starts with
The player's current score
The player's name
The number of enemies still alive
tasks.fb: The starting number of lives is decided by the programmer; the other three change as the game is played.

tasks.q: What data type does input() give the program?
a: A string
An integer
A Boolean
A real number
tasks.fb: Even if the user types 12, it arrives as the characters 1 and 2.

tasks.q: A program must add 1 to a number the user has typed. What has to happen first?
a: The input must be cast to an integer
The input must be printed
The input must be stored in a constant
The input must be placed inside a loop
tasks.fb: Arithmetic cannot be done on a string, so cast it to a number first.

a: Statements are carried out one after another in the order they are written
Statements are repeated until a condition is met
A choice is made between two sets of statements
Statements run in whichever order the computer finds quickest
tasks.fb: Nothing is skipped and nothing is repeated: each line runs once, in order.

tasks.q: What is wrong with this sequence:  print(total)  then  total = price * 2 ?
a: total is output before it has been given a value
print cannot be used with a variable
There are too few lines in the program
total should have been a constant
tasks.fb: Swapping the two lines fixes it: assign first, then use.

tasks.q: What does selection let a program do?
a: Choose between different sets of statements by testing a condition
Repeat a set of statements a fixed number of times
Store a value in memory under a name
Run every statement in the order written
tasks.fb: Selection is a choice at a fork in the road; iteration is a loop.

tasks.q: mark = 40. What does  if mark > 40 then print("Pass") else print("Fail") endif  output?
a: Fail
Pass
Nothing at all
tasks.fb: 40 is not greater than 40, so the else branch runs. The test should have been >= 40.

tasks.q: How many times does  for i = 0 to 9  repeat its block?
a: It depends on the starting value of i
tasks.fb: Both 0 and 9 are included, so that is ten repeats.

tasks.q: Which loop keeps asking for a password until the correct one is typed?
a: A condition-controlled loop
A count-controlled loop
A sequence
A constant
tasks.fb: You cannot know how many attempts the user will need, so a condition must control the loop.

tasks.q: Which construct does each line show?
tasks.fb: A line that just gets on with it is sequence; a line that asks a question is selection; a line that goes back is iteration.

tasks.q: Which construct does  while lives > 0  use?
a: Condition-controlled iteration
Count-controlled iteration
Selection
Sequence
tasks.fb: The number of repeats depends on a condition, not on a count.

info.title: Named in memory
info.text: A variable name is really a label for a memory location, and the computer works with the address rather than the name. Meaningful names like totalScore are not for the computer's benefit; they are for the next person to read your code.

info.title: Shouting case
info.text: Programmers often write constant names in capitals, such as MAX_LIVES, as a signal that nothing should change them. Python does not enforce this, so the capital letters are a promise between programmers.

info.title: Where output goes
info.text: Output does not have to be the screen. A program can output to a file, a printer, a speaker or another program, and the same data can go to several of them at once.

info.title: Sequence bugs
info.text: If two lines are swapped, the program usually still runs but gives the wrong answer. That is a logic error, not a syntax error, and no computer can spot it for you.

info.title: Nesting
info.text: An if can be placed inside another if, which is called nesting. It lets a program test a second condition only when the first one was True, like asking for a password only after a username matched.

info.title: Infinite loops
info.text: If nothing inside a condition-controlled loop ever makes the condition False, the loop never ends. Always change the variable the condition depends on, somewhere inside the loop.

diagrams.title: Sequence, selection and iteration
diagrams.text: The order the lines run in is not the order they are written in. Watch the program counter drop straight through, jump over a block, and jump back.
